claims.text: A high-entropy alloy contains at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 at.% each.
Effective valence electron count is a primary control on superconducting behavior in the proposed non-Nb–Ta-dominated HEA.
Lattice distortion is a primary control on superconducting behavior in the proposed HEA.
Increasing Ti content adjusts the effective valence electron count.
Increasing Ti content induces additional lattice distortion in the disordered BCC or near-BCC phase.
Ti enrichment enhances the local electronic density of states.
Ti enrichment adjusts the local bonding environment in the disordered BCC or near-BCC solid solution.
Additional lattice distortion enhances electron–phonon coupling.
The superconducting state of a relevant Ti-containing disordered HEA can be described within a weak-coupling BCS electron–phonon framework.
The proposed increase in electron–phonon coupling and density of states produces a higher superconducting transition temperature.
The proposed increase in electron–phonon coupling and density of states produces a higher upper critical field.
Increasing Ti content in the proposed HEA will raise Tc relative to an Nb–Ta-dominated HEA.
Increasing Ti content in the proposed HEA may raise Hc2 relative to an Nb–Ta-dominated HEA.
Previously studied BCC type-A HEA superconductors have Tc values of approximately 4.0–9.2 K.
Previously studied BCC type-A HEA superconductors can have upper critical fields close to 12 T.
Most previously studied type-A HEA superconductors contain large amounts of Nb and Ta and less than 20 at.% Ti.
Titanium-rich ternary and quaternary Nb–Ti-based alloys have shown the highest Hc2 values within the cited comparison sets.
The proposed Ti–superconductivity relationship applies only while a single-phase disordered BCC or near-BCC structure is retained.
Formation of ordered intermetallic compounds can invalidate the proposed relationship between Ti content and superconducting properties.
High-energy mechanical milling followed by sintering can ensure a uniform, disordered solid-solution phase in the proposed alloy series.

contradictions.description: The stated starting material is a non-Nb–Ta-dominated, Ti-rich HEA, but the outcome and falsification test compare it with a separate Nb–Ta-dominated HEA rather than with the starting material. This is not the requested controlled comparison and introduces composition-system confounding.

Ti atomic fraction cannot be increased while the concentrations of every other element are held constant, because normalized atomic percentages must sum to 100. Varying Ti is also incompatible with keeping the series equiatomic unless a specific substitution scheme is defined.

The boundary excludes phase-separated or ordered samples from the hypothesis's domain, whereas the falsification rule treats phase separation or ordered-compound formation as falsification. Leaving the stated applicability domain is not by itself a decisive test of the mechanism.

The hypothesis predicts both higher Tc and increased Hc2, while the predicted-outcome field weakens Hc2 to only a potential increase; the falsification rule nevertheless allows failure of either response to falsify the hypothesis.
